## Problem 1
```{r setup, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE}
library(p8105.datasets)
library(patchwork)
library(tidyverse)

library(knitr)
options(digits = 2)
data("ny_noaa")
```

```{r}
noaa_df = ny_noaa %>% 
  janitor::clean_names()

dim(noaa_df)

na_count <- noaa_df %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ mean(is.na(.)) * 100 ))
```

This dataframe contains `r nrow(noaa_df)` rows and `r ncol(noaa_df)` columns. The key variables include date, prcp (the amount of precipitation that day, in tenths of mm) snow (in mm), snwd (depth of the snow that day, in mm) tmax and tmin (the maximum and minimum temperatures that day in tenths of degrees C). Missing data is an issue here, as every weather station does not collect every value. Accordingly, `r pull(na_count, snow)`% of the snow data, `r pull(na_count, snwd)`% of snow depth, and `r pull(na_count, tmin)`% of both temp min and temp max data are missing.


```{r}
noaa_df = noaa_df %>% 
  mutate(
    day = lubridate::day(date),
    month = lubridate::month(date),
    year = lubridate::year(date),
    snow = ifelse(
      snow < 0, NA, snow
    ),
    prcp = prcp / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10,
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10
  )

noaa_df %>% 
  count(snow, name = "n_obs") %>% 
  arrange(desc(n_obs))

```
We add day, month, and year columns. Snow values less than 0 were changed to be NAs. We then adjust the prcp, tmax, and tmin to be full mm and degrees C, respectively. The majority of counts for snowfall were 0, since it does not snow in most places on most days.

```{r}
ggp_monthly_temp = noaa_df %>%
  filter(
    month %in% c(1, 7)
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    month = ifelse(
      month == 1, "January", "July"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(id, month, year) %>%
  summarize(
    avg_max = mean(tmax)
  )  %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = avg_max)) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~ month, ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Temperature by Station and Month",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Average Monthly Temperature (C)"
  )
  
ggp_monthly_temp
```
The plots of average temperatures in January and July show relatively consistent temperatures, with a few outliers (e.g. one very cold day in July in the late 1980s).


```{r}
ggp_full_tmp = noaa_df %>%
  pivot_longer(
    tmax:tmin,
    names_to = "observation", 
    values_to = "temp") %>%  
  ggplot(aes(x = temp, fill = observation)) +
  geom_density(alpha = .5) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Temperature by Station and Month",
    x = "Temperature (C)",
    y = "Density"
  )

ggp_snowfall = noaa_df %>% 
  filter(
    snow > 0 & snow < 100
  ) %>% 
  count(year, name = "snow_count") %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y=snow_count)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Snowfall Amounts",
    x = "# of Snowfalls between 0 and 100mm",
    y = "Year"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position="none")
  

ggp_full_tmp + ggp_snowfall
```
We made two density plots. The left compares minimum and maximum temperature by station and month, while the right shows how often stations recorded days with snowfalls between 0 and 100 millimeters by year.

## Problem 2
```{r}
accel_df = read.csv("./files/nhanes_accel.csv") %>% 
  janitor::clean_names() %>% 
  pivot_longer(
    min1:min1440,
    names_to = "minute", 
    values_to = "mims"
    )
covar_df = read.csv("./files/nhanes_covar.csv", skip = 4) %>% 
  janitor::clean_names() %>% 
  mutate(
    sex = as.factor(ifelse(sex == 1, "Male", "Female")), 
    education = as.factor(case_match(
      education,
        1 ~ "Less than high school",
        2 ~ "High school",
        3 ~ "More than high school"
      ))
  )

mims_df = accel_df %>% 
  left_join(covar_df, 'seqn')

head(mims_df, 5)
```

We load and tidy the datasets, pivoting the minutes into their own rows for the acceleration csv and changing from codes to male and female. We then left join them on the 'seqn' column. 

```{r}
mims_df = mims_df %>% 
  filter(age >= 21) %>%
  group_by(seqn) %>% 
  filter(!any(if_any(everything(), is.na))) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(
    education = as.factor(education),
    minute = as.numeric(str_remove(minute, "^min"))
  )
head(mims_df)
```
Education and minute are changed to factors, and rows for people under 21 years old are removed. We also remove any participants with na values.

```{r}
education_table <- mims_df %>%
  count(education, sex) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = sex,
    values_from = n,
    values_fill = 0
  ) %>%
  mutate(Total = Male + Female) %>%
  arrange(education)

kable(
  education_table,
  col.names = c("Education", "Men", "Women", "Total")
)

```

We create a chart with education levels by sex, along with totals. The largest category is More than high school. 

```{r}
ggplot(
  mims_df,
  aes(x = sex, y = age, fill = sex)
) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ education) +
  labs(
    title = "Age Distribution by Sex and Education",
    x = "Sex",
    y = "Age (years)",
    fill = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

The people with more than a high school education are generally younger than the other education levels. Among people with a high school education, the females with  were older than the males.  

```{r}
activity_totals <- mims_df %>%
  group_by(seqn, sex, age, education) %>%
  summarise(
    total_activity = sum(mims),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(activity_totals,
       aes(x = age, y = total_activity, color = sex)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~ education) +
  labs(
    title = "Total Activity by Age, Sex, and Education",
    x = "Age (years)",
    y = "Total Activity (MIMS)",
    color = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
As age increases, total activity decreases across all education levels and sexes. Women tended to do more activity than men for groups with at least a high school education, while the opposite was generally true for people with less than a high school education. 

```{r}
activity_by_minute <- mims_df %>%
  group_by(education, sex, minute) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_mims = mean(mims),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(activity_by_minute,
       aes(x = minute / 60,
           y = mean_mims)) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.8,
    aes(color = sex),
    alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(
    aes(color = sex), 
    method = "loess",
    span = 0.08,
    se = FALSE,
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Male" = "#1565C0", "Female" = "#E65100")) +
  facet_wrap(~ education, ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 4),
    limits = c(0, 24)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "24-Hour Activity Patterns by Education and Sex",
    x = "Time of Day (Hours)",
    y = "Mean Activity (MIMS)",
    color = "Sex"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

```
The plots of 24 hour activity show low activity in the early morning, with generally sustained energy throughout the middle of the day and into the night.
